title: The polished style of Hebrews compared with Paul's plain speech
english: The Epistle to the Hebrews does not have the untrained-in-speech quality of the Apostle in its style, even though he confessed that he was untrained in speech—that is, in wording. Rather, anyone who knows how to judge differences in wording would agree that the epistle is more Greek in the composition of its wording. And again, anyone who attends to the apostolic reading would also agree that this is true: the thoughts of the epistle are wonderful and not second to the acknowledged apostolic writings.
